summary: [workstream] assessment accepted as evidence for the W2 decision package ([branch]); no implementation or gameplay-change approval. Director feedback for the W1/W2 consolidation: (1) Progression: accept that the D-036 Casual 3–4 week target is not met. Keep core progression relatively fast: no slowing through grind, price inflation or economy-value changes. Extend *meaningful* progression through Galactic Projects, discoveries, collections and permanent world change; Active players must keep goals after 12★. Distinguish *longer progression* from *better engagement*: longer time-to-reward does not by itself improve retention. (2) Discovery: delivery-count thresholds are structurally unfit as the main mechanism. O4d (at most one guaranteed discovery per played day) is the W2 evaluation baseline, not a final decision. Conditions: presented as the result of delivery activity, not a login reward; no daily-login obligation, streak, absence penalty or FOMO; missed days never forfeit the next discovery; chapters stay completable after changing sector and never lock permanently because an earlier sector is inactive; evaluate whether Active players still feel progress rather than waiting for the day to change. No implementation before final approval. (3) Galactic Projects: the main long-term progression candidate, but never only a Credits sink or another progress bar. Each major project needs a clear goal, contributions that never block core purchases, visible progress, a permanent world change or clear reward, and a sensible tie to the galaxy, a sector or the Home Station. Evaluate P1 + re-gated P2 + P6.1–6.2 as the MLG candidate (not final). Surplus-only funding is evidence, not a validated rule: design a contribution mechanism players understand, then re-simulate to keep core-milestone delay within ±10 %. (4) Star-3 and HUD: Option A+ is the preferred option (visibility, recommended rocket-class hint, come-back-later message); no change to unlock requirements or contract cadence. The HUD mark hint is a priority UX fix (low-effort players cannot find Mk upgrades). SectorStars is a proposed rule type, with a compatibility review before implementation. UI guidance must clarify choices, not add management complexity. (5) Evidence classes in the W2 package: SIMULATED (EconomySim runs done), MODELLED (combined GP + discoveries + collection framing projections), UNVALIDATED (engagement, enjoyment, retention assumptions needing player tests). Never claim the Casual 3–4 week target is met by optimistically summing model results. Include the lightest, fastest next validation steps, including how to test whether post-12★ activity is genuinely engaging.
